_README: This file is normally WRITTEN FOR YOU by tools/calibrate_position_anchors.py.
Edit it by hand only if you cannot run that tool.
The two 'anchor' values are the seat centres in NORMALISED image
coordinates: x and y as a fraction of frame width and height, so the
file survives a resolution change. The values below are PLACEHOLDERS
and will not match your camera - replace them.
SCOPE: these are image coordinates. They are valid only while the
assembly sits in a fixed orientation on the fixture and the camera
does not move. Re-calibrate after any camera or fixture change.

_backend_options.geometric: nearest calibrated seat anchor. No training needed, fully interpretable, names which hole is wrong. Use this first.
_backend_options.classifier: the trained correct/wrong_position model decides. Needs train_position_model.py to have been run.
_backend_options.both: geometric and classifier must AGREE before a stage is held back. Use this for the recorded validation runs.

Seat_1.label: 1st hole
Seat_1.description: the hole the FIRST bushing goes into

Seat_2.label: 2nd hole
Seat_2.description: the hole the SECOND bushing goes into

_stage_requirements_note: Stages not listed here have no seat requirement; the validator reports NOT_APPLICABLE and never blocks them.
_max_anchor_distance_px_note: PLACEHOLDER ONLY. The calibration tool derives the gate as 40% of measured seat separation, strictly below half the separation so the two acceptance regions do not overlap. Do not use this template's anchor coordinates as real calibration.
_stability_note: Stability governs whether the OPERATOR is warned, never whether a stage may confirm. Any wrong verdict defers a confirmation immediately - a deferred stage costs one frame, a wrongly confirmed one poisons the baseline every later stage is judged against.
_require_seat_evidence_note: When true, a stage whose required seat has never once been seen filled is held back rather than confirmed on class counts alone. This is what makes 'Stage_01 must not confirm with the bushing in the wrong hole' true in both directions. Turn it off only if the detector genuinely cannot see a seated bushing; the manual stage keys [1]-[7] remain the documented override.

provenance.feasibility_note: POS-FEAS-01 is a synthetic CAD observability study (3.38% seat-region change at 35 deg). It is NOT a measurement of real-camera accuracy. No accuracy figure may be quoted for this feature until a labelled real-camera test set has been measured.
provenance.scope_note: Seat anchors originate from the saved calibration view. Runtime now tracks body_a image features frame-to-frame and transforms the two seat markers with it. Keep body_a visible and begin from the calibrated view; gradual image-plane movement is supported. This is not general 6-DoF pose estimation. If the view changes too much or tracking confidence is low, markers are hidden and Stage_01/02 position confirmation is paused. Recalibrate after moving the camera or changing resolution.

_pose_tracking_note: Body-relative feature tracking follows Seat_1/Seat_2 as the body moves. If tracking confidence drops, markers are hidden and Stage_01/02 confirmation is blocked; this is not a full 6-DoF pose estimator.
